classification.difficultyReason: Justify similarity from equal angles, identify adjacent and hypotenuse across orientations, then connect equal calculated ratios and a calculator value to the stated generalisation for all such triangles.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 2, three figures above part a
spec.description: Three unshaded right-angled triangles in source order, preserving their distinct orientations, 60° angles, right-angle marks and external dimension arrows. Decorative pale-blue source fills are omitted.
spec.mathematics: Left: adjacent 4 cm and hypotenuse 8 cm. Middle: adjacent 3.5 cm and hypotenuse 7 cm. Right: adjacent 5 cm and hypotenuse 10 cm. Each marked acute angle is 60°. Geometry is derived from these measurements.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Explain why these three triangles are similar.

answer.short: They all have angles of $90^{\circ}$, $60^{\circ}$ and $30^{\circ}$.
answer.worked: The third angle in each triangle is $180^{\circ}-90^{\circ}-60^{\circ}=30^{\circ}$. Their corresponding angles are equal, so the triangles are similar by AA.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Calculate the ratio of $\dfrac{\text{Adjacent}}{\text{Hypotenuse}}$ for each of the triangles.

answer.short: All three cosine ratios are equal.
answer.worked: The adjacent-to-hypotenuse ratio is $\dfrac12$ in all three triangles, despite their different sizes and orientations.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Type $\cos 60^{\circ}$ in your calculator. What does this tell you about $\dfrac{\text{Adjacent}}{\text{Hypotenuse}}$ for any right-angled triangle with a $60^{\circ}$ angle?

answer.worked: In degree mode, $\cos 60^{\circ}=0.5=\dfrac12$. Since $\cos\theta=\dfrac{\text{Adjacent}}{\text{Hypotenuse}}$, this ratio is always $\dfrac12$ for a right-angled triangle with a $60^{\circ}$ angle.
